header.title: Technology Enhanced Learning in Project-based Learning (TELIP)
header.subtitle: The Next Decade of Interdisciplinary Project-based Learning in Higher Education and at the Workplace: Outlining a TEL-Research Agenda

about.title: About the workshop

lead.text: The TELIP workshop brings together researchers and practitioners to map the next decade of TEL research on interdisciplinary project-based learning (iPBL) in higher education and at the workplace. Drawing on case presentations and structured group work, participants will identify practical challenges, outline a shared research agenda, and establish collaboration networks.

lead.title: Description
lead.text: To address today’s grand societal challenges, it is essential to promote learners working effectively across disciplinary boundaries. The prevalence of terms like multi-, inter- and transdisciplinary, or interprofessional learning illustrate this point. These forms of cross-boundary learning, subsumed under the term interdisciplinary learning in the following, often emerge through temporary project-based learning and working on shared challenges, whether in higher education by bringing together students from diverse academic backgrounds (e.g., project-based learning in interdisciplinary MSc study program) or in the workplace through forming cross-functional innovation teams (e.g., Dutch interprofessional learning communities to foster challenges in energy transition).

Learning holds great potential for addressing complex challenges and fostering active team learning at the same time, provided it is effectively implemented and facilitated. This underscores the need to research effective technology-enhanced approaches to iPBL in higher education and at the workplace.

about.conference: TELIP is held at the Twenty-first European Conference on Technology Enhanced Learning (ECTEL 2026), themed Mindful TEL: Learning Technologies Shaped with Intention, in Valencia, Spain (14–18 September 2026).
about.audience: Researchers in CSCL/CSCW, learning analytics, AI, and boundary-crossing work, together with practitioners (e.g., managers, teachers, coaches, and facilitators) involved in interdisciplinary project-based learning.
outcomes: Identification of practical challenges of interdisciplinary project-based learning in higher education and at the workplace with the help of case presentations, and clarification (dis)similarities between both application domains in a plenary discussion with all participants
Outline of a research agenda for understanding and supporting interdisciplinary project-based learning in the subgroups, and decision on the most relevant research questions by voting in the plenum
Foundations for co-authoring an agenda article and forming project consortia

topics.title: Topics & goals
topics: Team development, reflexivity, and dynamics in interdisciplinary teams
Epistemic awareness and boundary crossing across disciplines
Collaborative knowledge building and metacognitive scaffolding
Learning analytics and AI for team-based learning
Organisational scaling and sustainability of interdisciplinary learning
goals: Identify practical challenges of iPBL in higher education and workplace settings
Clarify similarities and differences across application domains
Outline a research agenda through structured subgroup work
Decide on priority research questions via plenary voting
Initiate co-authorship of an agenda article and project consortia formation

format.title: Workshop format
format.intro: TELIP is a three-part hybrid workshop combining plenary sessions and breakout work:
steps: Case presentations: Challenge identification from real iPBL cases in higher education and workplace contexts.
Research agenda formulation: structured breakout groups translate challenges into research directions.
Synthesis & planning: working-group presentations, voting in plenum on priority questions, and follow-up planning for publications and consortia.
